body.rationale: The governing IPS is still a draft, so I treated its limits as provisional but still informative. My picks favor portfolios the CIO can build from: ones that pass or nearly pass the IPS and rely on the covariance structure and tail risk rather than raw return forecasts, in line with the late-cycle finding in section 4.3. First choice is resampled_efficient_frontier. It has no hard breaches and 13.3 effective assets, and the best-diversified book that is still IPS-compliant. Its reviewers found the numbers consistent. The weaknesses are thin drawdown headroom (-24.3% vs -25%) and an unclear gamma description. Second is cvar_minimization. It also has no breaches and a backtest Sharpe of 0.74, and it handles skew and fat tails directly. The risk is that it is fitted to a few crises and tuned to the volatility edge. Third is pc_researcher. It has the second-highest ex-ante Sharpe (0.51), a backtest Sharpe of 0.70 and only two soft breaches (volatility, tracking error), with a modest -10.9% drawdown. It is a useful bridge between the compliant and low-risk groups, though the review noted that the delivered portfolio contradicts the narrative. Fourth is tail_risk_parity. It spans a different family from the first three picks, has 6.0 effective assets and a -7.2% drawdown, and offers defensive ballast. Its cash-heavy shape means it breaches return, volatility and tracking error. Its reviewers found the execution coherent. Fifth is max_sharpe. It is IPS-compliant with the best ex-ante Sharpe among compliant portfolios (0.46). The 46% in us_value rests on one judged CMA gap, which is the reason it ranks last. Why the first choice beats the fifth: resampled_efficient_frontier gets similar return and compliance with far better diversification (13.3 vs 3.8 effective assets), so it is far less exposed to a single CMA gap. I left out equal_weight, market_cap_weight and volatility_targeting because of drawdown breaches. I left out the cash-dominated inverse_variance, maximum_diversification and risk_parity because each breaches return, volatility and tracking error together. I flagged hierarchical_risk_parity. It is 92% cash, with one hard-breach set across three limits, effective N of 1.4, and a review-identified technical error. The CIO should not lean on it. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier, since its orthogonality has value in an ensemble.
